Name: Obj_NoContemporaryRomanRecord
Statement: A provincial was executed under a prefect of Judaea, and you tell me the world turned on it. Then show me the world noticing. Where is the record made at the time, by someone with no stake in the outcome?
ConcededResponse: A senator who despises you, and a stone with the man's own title cut into it. That is not nothing. I will grant you the execution.
PressedResponse: So: nothing written at the time, by anyone, anywhere. You are asking me to take the movement's word for the movement's founding.

Name: Obj_TestimoniumIsInterpolated
Statement: You lean on Josephus. I have read the passage you mean. No Jew of his standing wrote those words about a man he did not follow -- somebody has been at the text. If that is your independent witness, your independent witness has been improved.
ConcededResponse: The other passage, then. The brother, and the execution under the high priest. That one nobody has tampered with, and it is mentioned in passing, which is harder to forge.
PressedResponse: Then you have no answer, and you are still quoting a passage you know has been handled.

Name: Obj_PublicOrderNotTruth
Statement: I am not interested in whether it is true. I am interested in unlicensed assemblies, refusals of the customary offering, and riots in my jurisdiction. Give me one reason to treat this as anything but a disorder.
ConcededResponse: A governor put exactly that question to the emperor and came back with nothing criminal beyond the name itself. Very well. The name is not yet a crime in this court.
PressedResponse: Then it is a disorder, and I will treat it as one.

Name: Obj_WomenWitnessesWouldNotStandInCourt
Statement: Your first witnesses are women. I do not say this to insult them. I say it because you know as well as I do what weight that testimony carries in any court between here and Rome. You have built on ground no advocate would choose.
ConcededResponse: No advocate would choose it. Which is your point, and it is a better one than I would like.
PressedResponse: You have not even a reason why they are there. You simply repeat that they are.

Name: Obj_AppearancesWereGriefVisions
Statement: Grieving men see the dead. It is common, it is well attested, and it costs nothing to explain. What have you that a grief-vision does not account for?
ConcededResponse: Groups, and not all at once, and one of them a man who was hunting them at the time. Grief does not explain the last of those. I will hear the rest.
PressedResponse: Then grief explains it, and we are finished.

Name: Obj_CrucifiedMessiahIsAScandal
Statement: I have read the Law my whole life. What you are proclaiming is not merely unlikely, it is shameful -- and you proclaim it in the streets as though shame were the point. No one invents a messiah who ends on a Roman cross. So either you are fools, or something happened that you cannot get around.
ConcededResponse: And it is the crucifixion that stands at the head of the form you hand on, not buried in it. You did not grow into that claim. You started there.
PressedResponse: Then you cannot tell me why you are saying the one thing guaranteed to lose you a hearing, and I am left with fools.

Name: Obj_FortyYearsOfDrift
Statement: Nothing was written for a generation. I have watched a story cross three villages and come back unrecognisable. You are asking me to believe that forty years of mouths changed nothing.
ConcededResponse: A set form, fixed early, handed on word for word by men trained to do exactly that -- and the people named in it still alive to be asked. That is not village talk. I concede it.
PressedResponse: Forty years, then, and nothing to show it was held steady. That is a long time for a story to be on its own.

Name: Obj_CreedIsPaulsOwnWork
Statement: You call it early because Paul hands it on. But Paul is the one writing. How do you know he received it, rather than composed it and dressed it as tradition to give it weight?
ConcededResponse: Words he does not use elsewhere, a shape built for memorising, and by his own account he was sitting with Peter within a few years of it. That is a received thing. Yes.
PressedResponse: Then your earliest evidence is a man asserting his own authority, which is what I said it was.

Name: Obj_GospelsAreAnonymous
Statement: Open any of the four and read to the end. Not one of them says who wrote it. The names were put on the outside by people who were not there. You are arguing from titles.
ConcededResponse: Named by a man two generations back, and named the same way everywhere afterwards, with no competing claim anywhere. For an anonymous work that is a strange kind of unanimity.
PressedResponse: Four books that do not name themselves, and you have nobody early who names them either.

Name: Obj_MatthewAndLukeCopiedMark
Statement: Set the three side by side and read them in Greek. Two of them follow the third's order and keep his wording, down to his awkward constructions -- which a man improving a source does not preserve. They are copying. So Matthew did not write first, whatever the fathers say.
ConcededResponse: A collection of sayings in the Hebrew dialect, early, and the Greek book that carries his name later and after Mark. Two different documents. That I can hold alongside what I read in the text.
PressedResponse: You are repeating a tradition without answering the pages in front of you.

Name: Obj_TraditionIsUnanimousOnMatthewFirst
Statement: Every man who was close enough to know says Matthew was first, and they say it independently, in different provinces, across a century. You have a theory about word order. They had the churches that kept the books.
ConcededResponse: And what they were told was first was the sayings in the Hebrew dialect, which is exactly what the tradition says. The Greek book is another matter. Good -- then we are not as far apart as I was told.
PressedResponse: So you set aside every early witness on the strength of a reconstruction nobody made until recently.

Name: Obj_LukeWroteTooLateToHaveAsked
Statement: Your physician says he investigated eyewitnesses. By the time most date his book, the eyewitnesses are dead. A man may say he made enquiries. Show me he was in a position to make them.
ConcededResponse: His second book stops dead at a house arrest, before the fire, before the Temple came down, and mentions none of it. That is a hard thing to explain in a late writer. I will allow he may have been early enough.
PressedResponse: A stated method and no way to check it is a claim, not a source.

Name: Obj_LukeHasBeenEdited
Statement: The gospel you read has been added to. I have the older, shorter book, and the additions are exactly where you would expect a Jewish hand to have been at work. You are defending an expanded text and calling it original.
ConcededResponse: Copies older than your teacher, agreeing with the fourth-century books almost line for line. It is your text that is the edition, and everyone can now see where the knife went in.
PressedResponse: Then you cannot show me a copy older than the cutting, and we are both holding editions.

Name: Obj_LongerEndingProvesTampering
Statement: The last twelve verses of Mark are not in your best copies, and they do not sound like the rest of the book. Something was added. Once I know a hand has been in the text, why should I trust any of it?
ConcededResponse: You know it was added because the copies are early enough and many enough to show you the seam. A tradition thin enough to be quietly rewritten would never have caught it. I take the point, though I do not like it.
PressedResponse: An addition you cannot account for, in the earliest of your gospels, at the most important place in it.

Name: Obj_PapiasIsLateAndDismissed
Statement: Your whole case for Mark rests on Papias. He wrote two generations after the fact, his book is lost, and the very historian who preserves the fragment tells us he was a man of small understanding. That is your foundation.
ConcededResponse: Irenaeus knew of him a century and a half before that judgement was passed, and rated his access highly. The dismissal is later than the man. Fair.
PressedResponse: Then you are resting on a witness his own editor thought a fool.

Name: Obj_IrenaeusAndClementDisagreeOnMark
Statement: Your two best witnesses to when Mark wrote contradict each other. One puts it after Peter was dead, the other has Peter alive and approving. They cannot both be right, and you have no way to choose.
ConcededResponse: They disagree about the year and agree about the man. Nobody in either account thinks Mark got it from anyone but Peter. That is the part I was asking about.
PressedResponse: So your tradition cannot keep its story straight within a century of the event.
